thread:
maria: FYI CI linkcheck failed on the latest docs deploy, reproducible on my machine. it flags several internal anchors as 404s even though they render in the browser :thinking:
ben: can you paste the failing excerpt from the linkcheck job?
maria: here's the snippet from the GH Actions log:
```
LinkCheck: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/usage#installing-the-sdk -> 404 (fragment not found)
LinkCheck: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/model-routing#route-priorities -> 404 (fragment mismatch)
```
ben: hmm those anchors look present in the HTML, so it's probably a mismatch between generated slug vs link text. any special chars in headings?
maria: yes — one heading contains an inline code span: `--prefer-quantization` and another has a trailing emoji :gear:. I bet the slugifier is removing/transforming those differently than link authoring assumed.
oliver: relates to the markdown renderer we switched to during the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration. docusaurus slugify uses a different normalizer for inline code and emoji. we saw a few of these in the early migration run.
ben: quick workaround: we can change the in-doc link to point at the explicit heading id (add `{#install-sdk}`) or update the heading to a simpler slug. long-term we should normalize slug generation so linkcheck and writers agree.
celine: i can do a small PR to normalize headings during build: add a remark plugin to strip emojis and collapse inline code in slug generation. that should keep visible heading text but stable IDs. want me to open it?
maria: please. also can we add a linkcheck whitelist for known-redirects so CI doesn't fail noisy for a short window?
ben: +1 for whitelist, but prefer fixing slug generation first. if celine opens a draft PR i can add a minor SDK docs change (replace inline code link targets) so the immediate failing jobs pass.
docs-bot: Deploy preview for PR #4321 available at https://deploy-preview-4321--docs.redwood.ai/ :eyes:
oliver: celine, for the remark plugin config, make sure to run slug generation on both Markdown headings and explicit link refs. we have a few places where authors used `[install](#installing-the-sdk)` vs raw links to generated ids. unify behavior.
celine: noted. I'll include tests that run `node ./scripts/slugcheck.js` locally, and add a GH Action step that compares generated anchors to link refs to catch regressions.
maria: if you want me to pre-fix the immediate pages, tell me which files. I can do a tiny mass-replace sed for the inline-code->explicit-id links and push a hotfix PR.
ben: list: `docs/sdk/getting-started.md`, `docs/guides/model-routing.md`, `docs/ops/latency-tuning.md` — those hit linkcheck in the last 3 failures.
celine: I'll open the slugifier PR first and add the unit tests. maria, if you open the hotfix PR after that (or before if it unblocks CI), ping me and I'll rebase if needed.
maria: will open hotfix now with the three quick link edits. PR title: "docs: fix broken fragment links (temp hotfix)" — assigning to ben for review.
ben: taking it. also will add a short README note in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md about adding explicit `{#id}` when inline code is part of the heading until slugifier lands.
oliver: one more ask — can we add a check in the preview bot comment linking the page + anchor, so reviewers can click straight to the fragment? small UX win.
docs-bot: Added preview comment to PR #4322 with direct fragment links.
maria: awesome — thanks everyone. i'll watch the CI run and post back if something else pops up. :thumbsup:
ben: thanks — sounds like a plan.
celine: will tag you all on the slugifier PR when draft ready.
(maria edited message)
